up.note: Two textbook steps. First $\mathrm{NS}_\delta(f)\le\delta\,\mathrm{I}(f)$ (a union bound over which coordinate is pivotal), so the threshold $\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}\ge\mathrm{Var}/4$ defining $\delta^{*}$ cannot be reached before $\delta = \mathrm{Var}/(4\mathrm{I})$, giving $\mathrm{nsr}\le 4\,\mathrm{I}(f)/\mathrm{Var}(f)$. Second, count sensitive edges: with $p = \Pr[f=1]\le\tfrac12$ (else complement, which changes neither side), $\mathrm{I}(f) = 2|\partial S|/2^n \le 2\,\mathrm{s}(f)\,p$ because every $x\in S=f^{-1}(1)$ has at most $\mathrm{s}(f)$ sensitive edges, while $\mathrm{Var}(f) = 4p(1-p)\ge 2p$. Hence $\mathrm{I}\le\mathrm{s}\cdot\mathrm{Var}$ and the $\mathrm{Var}$ cancels. By closure this also gives $\mathrm{nsr} = O(\mathrm{D})$; the constant $4$ is an artefact of the $\mathrm{Var}/4$ threshold convention in \(\mathrm{nsr}(f)\).

lo.note:
$\mathrm{NS}_\delta = (2+o(1))\,P\,(1-(1-\delta)^{3m-6})$ with
$P = m(m-1)(m-2)2^{6-3m}$ and $\mathrm{Var} = (4+o(1))P$, so the threshold
$\mathrm{Var}/4$ is crossed at $\delta^{*} = \Theta(1/m)$, against
$\mathrm{s} = 3m-6$. A sensitive-everywhere function is as noise-robust as its
sensitivity allows.

Hence $\mathrm{I}\le\mathrm{s}\cdot\mathrm{Var}$ and the $\mathrm{Var}$ cancels. Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{nsr}(\mathrm{SCORPION}_m) = \Theta(m) = \Theta(\mathrm{s})\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{SCORP}_m\)
    $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = (2+o(1))\,P\,(1-(1-\delta)^{3m-6})$ with $P = m(m-1)(m-2)2^{6-3m}$ and $\mathrm{Var} = (4+o(1))P$, so the threshold $\mathrm{Var}/4$ is crossed at $\delta^{*} = \Theta(1/m)$, against $\mathrm{s} = 3m-6$. A sensitive-everywhere function is as noise-robust as its sensitivity allows.

facts: $\mathrm{nsr}(f) = O(\mathrm{s}(f))$, hence $O(\mathrm{D}(f))$: for a balanced-or-lighter $f$ the edge count gives $\mathrm{I}(f)\le \mathrm{s}(f)\,\mathrm{Var}(f)$, and combining with the line above kills the $\mathrm{Var}$.

Incomparable to \(\mathrm{osss}(f)\), the other normalization of a dimensionless Fourier quantity: $\oplus_n$ has $\mathrm{osss} = 1$ but $\mathrm{nsr} = \Theta(n)$, and $\mathrm{MAJ}_n$ has $\mathrm{osss} = \Theta(\sqrt n)$ but $\mathrm{nsr} = \Theta(1)$.
Large $\mathrm{nsr}$ means robust, so it behaves oppositely to \(\mathrm{I}(f)\) on the same data: the two are the $\delta\to 0$ and $\delta\to\delta^{*}$ readings of the same curve.
self.name: Noise robustness
self.short: One over the noise rate at which f starts to break: the query-scale reading of NS_delta.
